comparator.name: Global Management of Social Issues
comparator.sourceNotes: The English-taught track has 60 EC each year. The third-year mobility window allows 30 EC of approved study or an internship, including specified combinations. Students complete a 12 EC individual thesis in the final semester.
components: GROW mentoring and personal development continue across the three years and carry no credits.
The ordinary first-year binding study advice threshold is 42 EC from the first-year curriculum.
History of Government and Public Institutions
Fundamentals of International Law and EU Law
Financial and Project Management, or equivalent prior knowledge, prepares students for this course’s work on projects involving multiple organisations and stakeholders.
Causal Analysis Techniques prepares students to analyse quantitative data and write a research paper. Working-group attendance is required.
Mobility Window: Approved Study or Internship

Choose 30 EC of approved study or an internship, or a permitted combination. Internships can carry 12, 18, 24 or 30 EC, with minor courses completing the balance. Study abroad can carry 30 EC, or 24 EC alongside a 6 EC Tilburg course.
Wicked Problems 301: Intervention Theories and Tools
The standard spring thesis requires at least 120 EC within the programme. Students conduct individual research with support from a thesis group and defend their work.

core: Wicked problems and organisational approaches to complex global social challenges
Organisation, human-resource management, collaboration and project leadership across cultures
Climate change and sustainability as social and organisational challenges
International organisations, global governance, law and social policy
Interdisciplinary social research, intervention and philosophical reflection
adjacent: Multistakeholder governance and humanitarian organisational response
questions: How can organisations and institutions coordinate responses to wicked global problems?
How do law, policy and governance shape responses to migration, poverty and inequality?
How can responsible management and social entrepreneurship address climate and social challenges?

selection.assessment: Three options address organisational responses to social problems, international policy and displacement, or sustainability and social entrepreneurship. Their different organising questions are sustained by distinct course selections.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Global social challenges, governance & organisations
alternatives.labelReason: Organisational behaviour, governance and social inquiry anchor the option, with international politics, law and public economics.
alternatives.concept: Study how organisations and institutions respond to complex social problems. Combine organisational psychology, negotiation and governance with international politics, law, public economics and empirical research.
progression: Research methods prepare for advanced survey research and econometrics. Law, Society & Justice precedes public international law. Introductory leadership and sociology support later organisational psychology and social theory.

alternatives.label: International policy, law & displacement
alternatives.labelReason: International and EU law, political institutions, conflict and social inquiry support analysis of policy responses to displacement.
alternatives.concept: Study how laws, institutions and policies shape international responses to social problems and displacement. Combine public international law and EU governance with conflict studies, historical analysis and social research.
alternatives.distinctness: Legal institutions, rights, public policy and historical inquiry are central here. The closest option focuses more on organisations, behaviour and empirical methods.
progression: Legal foundations precede international, EU and constitutional law. Comparative politics and research methods support advanced governance and policy inquiry.

alternatives.label: Sustainability, inequality & social entrepreneurship
alternatives.labelReason: Social inquiry, environmental justice, product development and strategy connect enterprise decisions to social and environmental challenges.
alternatives.concept: Explore how enterprises and communities respond to inequality and environmental pressures. Study customer needs, circular product design, digital strategy and social movements alongside economics, ethics and sustainability governance.
alternatives.distinctness: This option develops a sustained enterprise and sustainability focus, including product design, customer research and environmental justice. The other options focus on organisational coordination or international institutions.
progression: Sustainability foundations precede life-cycle analysis. Research methods prepare for marketing and leadership research, while business foundations precede digital strategy, transnational law and market research.

blocks: Both develop financial accounting and management skills. Tilburg also teaches project management.
Both introduce social-science research design, measurement and empirical analysis.
Both connect survey design, measurement and quantitative analysis. UCR applies these methods to leadership and social experience.
Both examine motivation, teams, leadership and culture within organisations.
Both introduce sociological theories and apply them to social questions.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation.
Both study social influence, group behaviour and psychological research.
Both develop statistical analysis for social or behavioural data.
Both introduce economic reasoning about markets, choices and public intervention.
Both use regression to investigate empirical relationships. UCR also teaches instrumental variables in economic applications.
Both study public international law and institutions. Tilburg also incorporates EU law.
Both examine organisational change. UCR focuses on digital strategy and transformation.

notes.text: Tilburg combines organisation studies, human resource management, international law and research through a sequence on wicked problems and a required individual thesis. UCR offers related courses across these fields, with different emphases in each option.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Management of Social Issues at Tilburg University studies how organisations respond to complex problems such as inequality, migration and climate change. Students combine organisation studies, human resource management, law and social research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study through organisational responses to social problems, international policy and displacement, or sustainability and social entrepreneurship. Tilburg integrates these fields through its wicked-problems sequence, cross-cultural management and required thesis.
